public.title: Strongly Connected Components
public.description: Given a directed graph with n vertices labeled 0 through n-1 and an array edges of pairs [from, to], return its strongly connected components. A component is a maximal group in which every vertex can reach every other vertex by following directed edges; a zero-edge path reaches the starting vertex itself. Sort the labels within each component numerically ascending, then sort components by their smallest label ascending. Include isolated vertices as singleton components. For n = 0 return []. Constraints: n is an integer from 0 to 200; edges has 0 to 1000 pairs of valid vertex labels (and must be empty when n = 0). Self-loops and repeated directed edges are allowed and do not change component membership. Edge input order has no effect on the result. Aim for linear graph traversal work, plus sorting to canonicalize the output.
hints: A traversal in the original graph gives a useful finishing order.
Traverse reversed edges in decreasing finishing order, collecting one component at a time.
Traversal order is not the required output order; canonicalize afterward.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and solutions, 2026. Uses standard graph algorithms; no third-party exercise text used.

explanation: Build the graph and its edge reversal. A first depth-first pass appends vertices after their descendants finish. A second pass on reversed edges processes vertices in decreasing finishing order; each newly reached group is exactly one strongly connected component. Sort each group numerically and the groups by their minimum label. Traversals take O(n + m) time, where m is the number of edge entries. Canonical sorting makes total time O(m + n log(n + 1)); adjacency lists, visited flags, traversal order, output and recursion use O(n + m) space. Recursion depth is at most the supported 200 vertices. Functional tests check membership and ordering, not asymptotic complexity.
